newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen disarms citizens toting illegal guns.
newsitem.headline: Yemen disarms citizens toting illegal guns.

text.p: Security forces were deployed in Yemen's major cities on Saturday in an attempt to disarm citizens who own a vast arsenal of unlicensed weapons.
Witnesses said forces patrolling city streets or positioned at traffic lights were searching cars and pedestrians for illicit arms.
"Our task is to disarm people who are not qualified to carry weapons," a member of the Central Security Forces in the capital Sanaa told Reuters.
The move comes less than a week after a gunman shot dead four children and two teachers at adjacent schools in Sanaa. The man is due to be executed in the capital on Saturday.
Since the shooting spree, which shocked and enraged the nation, articles in the official press have called for steps to cut down on the proliferation of unlicensed weapons.
Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh has also called on the interior ministry to beef up security measures ahead of parliamentary elections on April 27.

Saturday's issue of Al-Mu'tammar, the newspaper of Saleh's General People's Congress party, said the disarmament campaign had been launched in the capitals of Yemen's governorates and in cities throughout the country.
"The campaign came in order to maintain calm during the election process and to reduce crime in the country, especially after the incident at the schools," the paper said.
Illicit guns, predominantly Kalashnikov automatic rifles, are openly carried in Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest countries.
Unofficial estimates put the number of firearms in the country at nearly 50 million, three times the population of 16 million.
